name: Galton Box
miniText: How do repeated binary choices build a bell-shaped histogram? NetLogo Galton Box drops balls through rows of pegs, choosing left or right with a controllable probability and accumulating destination counts. Durrett [1] supplies binomial and limit-theorem foundations; Berry [2] quantifies approximation of sums by a Gaussian distribution; Wilensky [3] examines learning about normality through constructive simulation. The baseline illustrates how many paths can reach the same final position and how bias shifts the resulting distribution. Its decisions are probabilistic rules rather than simulated impacts with friction or elasticity. A finite number of rows gives a discrete distribution, while finite ball counts create sampling noise. Pile-up and display capacity also affect what remains visible. A normal approximation is conditional on the sum structure and parameter regime, rather than a universal property of random movement.
